additional_info.subject: Description
additional_info.body:
Hello,
Is it possible to check logs on the charger 170002644 on yesterday 7 of November at 2:39:07 p.m.; at 2:41:07 p.m.; at 3:30:47 p.m.; at 3:32:53 p.m.; at 3:34:01 p.m. (CU Time) ?
A customer tried to charge thru IPlanet App. Every recharge was authorized, but was a 0 recharge, also after a reboot.
Thank you in advance

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0460583-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP / R9 170002644] CU logs check CRM:00263000136
additional_info.body:
Dear Filomena,
I am following up in regards of ticket
ID0460583.
Here is a detailed analysis of the events reported:
As reported by my colleague Guilherme, the first session was authorized remotely:
2025-11-07T14:39:07.589393+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/98f22f472b97[822]: OCPP: Received command: RemoteStartTransaction (5312272) - {"connectorId":3,"idTag":"EV-000006167"}
2025-11-07T14:39:07.595293+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/98f22f472b97[822]: OCPP: Send result: RemoteStartTransaction (5312272) - {"status":"Accepted"}
2025-11-07T14:39:07.601197+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/98f22f472b97[822]: OCPP: Send command: Authorize (6b813d5c-62ba-43f0-9300-433deba80ef2) - {"idTag":"EV-000006167"}
2025-11-07T14:39:07.655534+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/98f22f472b97[822]: OCPP: Received result: Authorize (6b813d5c-62ba-43f0-9300-433deba80ef2) - {"idTagInfo":{"status":"Accepted"}
We see then the following log line:
2025-11-07T14:39:19.725173+00:00 [FW080005G1] swcpu [user:debug] [4322] [ACC]  AC1: 32A Cabel attached
This means that the AC cable was connected to the Charger, but we do not see any change in Pilostate. This means that the cable is either not connected from EV side, or the cable itself has a problem.
This behavior happened twice, as per logs in the picture:
After the reboot, the behavior is pretty much the same.
We see a very rapid change of Pilot state, which could mean either the customer plugged in in the vehicle and plugged out very quickly, or that the cable used is not working properly.
To summarize, I checked the behavior of the Ac socket and yesterday and the day before yesterday charged with no problem. Hence, I am assuming that the issue was either in the wrong handling of the session from the user, or that the user was using a damaged/not working AC cable.
Since the issue seems to appear being related to end user, if there are no further questions, I would proceed to close this ticket.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you!
